_comment_brand: The TypedSvg brand config — the phantom-typing layer elm-cem lays over the SVG CEM
manifest (../generated/package/elm-typed-svg/manifest/svg.cem.json). Same role and shape as the
html brand's config (../../html/inputs/config.json); read that first for the primitive vocabulary.
The ONE thing that makes this a distinct kind of brand: `_namespace`. SVG elements are not HTML
elements — a `<circle>` created with `document.createElement` (HTML namespace) does not render; it
elm-cem emitter to build every element ctor with `Ir.nodeNS "<uri>"` instead of `Ir.node`, which
routes through `VirtualDom.nodeNS` / `createElementNS`. This is the additive that the IR gained in
represented and this brand could not exist. Everything else here is ordinary phantom config.
_comment_renames: The `<text>` element's natural ctor name `text` collides with the shared text-content atom
`text` (both land at the top level of the `TypedSvg` barrel). elm/svg resolves the identical
clash the same way: the content function is `Svg.text` and the element is `Svg.text_`. So the
`<text>` element ctor is renamed to `text_`; the atom keeps the unsuffixed `text`.
_comment_globals: SVG presentation + core attributes. Unlike html — where most globals are CLOSED (in every
element's Attrs record) — nearly all SVG presentation attributes genuinely apply to every rendered
element (fill/stroke/opacity/transform are universal), so they are declared `"row": "open"`: an
open setter needs no per-element row membership to compose, so `TypedSvg.Attributes.fill` drops onto
any element by structural unification. This is the faithful model for SVG's global presentation
properties, and it is exactly the shape html uses for its five open globals (dir/lang/tabindex/...).
id/class/style are kept CLOSED (the default row), matching html: they reach every element via the
closed Attrs row and class/style carry the emitter's bespoke merging setters (classList/style p v).
A handful of small, closed-vocabulary presentation attributes are typed as enums (stroke-linecap,
stroke-linejoin, fill-rule, clip-rule, visibility, text-anchor) so a wrong token is a compile error;
the open lengths/colours/paints stay free strings (an SVG length is `10`, `50%`, or `10px`, and a
paint is a colour, `url(#id)`, `currentColor`, `none`, ... — no finite token set).
_comment_nesting: SVG's content model is deliberately permissive: container elements (svg, g, defs, symbol, a, switch,
pattern, mask, clipPath, marker) accept essentially any SVG content, so they admit `any`. Leaf shapes
admit only the accessibility descriptors title/desc. Gradients admit their `stop` children. Text
admits tspan/textPath runs plus the shared `text` content atom. Produced kinds default to the tag
name (a `stop` produces kind `stop`, admitted by a gradient's `["stop"]` slot), so most elements need
no explicit `kind` — only their `home` module grouping and `admits`.
_comment_foreignObject: `foreignObject` is the ONE typed bridge out of the SVG namespace into HTML. Its slot admits the
cross-library `shared:flow` / `shared:phrasing` content categories — the same roles every TypedHtml
flow/phrasing producer (`div`, `span`, ...) tags itself with — so an HTML subtree nests here by
structural unification, while a bare SVG shape (which produces its own tag kind, e.g. `circle`) is
rejected. That is the exact SVG-2 content-model boundary: HTML goes inside `foreignObject`, not inside
a `<circle>`. The element ctor itself is namespaced SVG (`createElementNS`), as every SVG element is.
_comment_filter: The SVG filter family (Task 5 of the API-spec audit): a `<filter>` container holding a graph of
`fe*` primitives, each producing a named `result` another consumes via `in`. All 26 elements live in
a single `Filter` home module (TypedSvg/Element/Filter.elm). Content model:
- `filter` admits `any` — SVG's filter content model accepts any filter primitive (plus desc/title),
and enumerating all 16 primitive kinds would be a brittle restatement of the home module itself.
- `feMerge` admits ONLY `feMergeNode` (its layer children); `feComponentTransfer` admits ONLY the
four `feFunc*` channel-transfer children; the two lighting primitives admit ONLY a light source
(`feDistantLight`/`fePointLight`/`feSpotLight`). These tight slots are the real content-model
fidelity — a wrong child there is a compile error.
- leaf primitives (blur/offset/flood/...) and the light sources are childless (no `admits`).
`color-interpolation-filters`) are open-row _globals above, alongside the other presentation props.
`feMorphology` operator, `feTurbulence` stitchTiles) are typed in the manifest as pipe-delimited
attribute value domains, so a bad token is a compile error.
